nodes.label: Read-Only Organization Access
nodes.rationale: The login experience states that dashboard access is read-only, secured by existing organization membership, and presents reconciled accounting data as the source of truth.

nodes.label: tb_ledger_balance_snapshots
nodes.rationale: Stores dated accounting baselines separately from mutable ledger master-data opening balances.

nodes.label: tb_history_coverage
nodes.rationale: Provides a small diagnostic contract so report entry points can reject unreconciled dates.

nodes.label: tb_ledger_voucher_lines
nodes.rationale: Uses the latest dated snapshot at or before each voucher so running balances remain historically stable.

nodes.label: tb_tally_trial_balance_snapshots
nodes.rationale: Preserves Tally's total-level trial balance, including rows that cannot be reconstructed from ledger closing balances.

nodes.label: tb_voucher_affects_books
nodes.rationale: Centralizes the authoritative definition of a voucher that posts to the books.

nodes.label: Accounting-eligible tb_trial_balance_verification
nodes.rationale: Excludes Closing Stock and Profit & Loss A/c because ledger closing balances are not authoritative for those calculated trial-balance rows.

nodes.label: All Order Voucher Exclusion
nodes.rationale: An order is an operational commitment rather than an accounting posting, so any voucher type ending in ' order' stays in raw data but outside the books.

nodes.label: Interactivity Isolation
nodes.rationale: Motion-heavy UI should live in microscopic client leaf components so server layouts remain static and continuous animation cannot rerender parents.

nodes.label: Step Sequence
nodes.rationale: Use numbered vertical stages when the product is a workflow rather than a single moment.

nodes.label: Annotated Screenshot
nodes.rationale: Use the product UI itself as the explanation, with arrows or concise labels identifying details.

nodes.label: Product Card Grid
nodes.rationale: Commerce layouts should use uniform product cards so visual rhythm comes from the products, not irregular feature-tile spans.

nodes.label: Mast-Headed Footer
nodes.rationale: A quiet singular footer lets heavy page content end with a wordmark, tagline, and only a few links.

nodes.label: Inline-Rule Single-Line Footer
nodes.rationale: An editorial page can treat the footer as an afterthought through one credit line and a hairline rule.

nodes.label: Index-Style Category Footer
nodes.rationale: Hubs and documentation roots benefit from short categorized navigation columns.

nodes.label: Dense Typographic Footer
nodes.rationale: A compact monospace colophon supports editorial brands when references and credits matter more than navigation.

nodes.label: Statement Footer
nodes.rationale: A large closing sentence should complete the page argument; it is unsuitable for documentation hubs where it reads as marketing fluff.

nodes.label: Letter-Close Footer
nodes.rationale: A warm editorial page can close like personal correspondence, but the voice clashes with stat-led B2B product pages.

nodes.label: Newsletter-First Footer
nodes.rationale: The subscription form may lead the footer only when the brand genuinely publishes and subscription was already offered above the fold.

nodes.label: Marquee-Scroll Footer
nodes.rationale: Kinetic repeated taglines suit loud sport, fashion, agency, or manifesto voices and must honor reduced-motion preferences.

nodes.label: Marquee Hero
nodes.rationale: A single statement can fill the fold when the brand or person is itself the message.

nodes.label: Split Diptych Hero
nodes.rationale: Pair each claim with visual proof by placing headline and lede beside an image or product capture.

nodes.label: Quote-Led Hero
nodes.rationale: A real testimonial can supply borrowed credibility strong enough to lead the front page.

nodes.label: Stat-Led Hero
nodes.rationale: One defensible externally verifiable metric can become the hero focal point.

nodes.label: Letter Hero
nodes.rationale: A first-person salutation without buttons suits a brand built around the founder's personal voice.

nodes.label: Photographic-Fold Hero
nodes.rationale: Real photography that can carry the page should receive a full-bleed viewport treatment.

nodes.label: Clipped Demo-Video Hero
nodes.rationale: Clipping part of a real product demo beyond the viewport suggests that the product contains more than the screen can show.

nodes.label: Browser-Framed Mockup Hero
nodes.rationale: A subtly tilted browser-frame mockup gives a web-app screenshot structure and visual life.

nodes.label: Custom Illustration Centerpiece Hero
nodes.rationale: A brand-specific craft, character, or process should be drawn as a hand-built SVG or CSS illustration rather than selected from a generic library.

nodes.label: Wordmark and Two-Link Navigation
nodes.rationale: A page with very few destinations needs only a wordmark and two text links, without a logo image or menu icon.

nodes.label: Floating-on-Scroll Morph Navigation
nodes.rationale: One sticky navigation DOM should morph from a bar into a floating pill with a single class toggle and timing curve.

nodes.label: Floating Navigation Four Laws
nodes.rationale: Keep height constant, offset with transforms, cross-fade all changing properties, and use one timing curve.

nodes.label: Single-DOM Navigation Crossfade
nodes.rationale: Swapping two header elements harms focus order and content synchronization; cross-fade one DOM instead.

nodes.label: Mega-Menu Panel
nodes.rationale: Use for brands with many destinations that require grouped explanations; constrain the panel to about four columns and 60vh, provide close grace, keyboard closure, synchronized scrim state, and a mobile accordion drawer.

nodes.label: Announcement Banner and Retracting Nav
nodes.rationale: Use for a genuine time-bound announcement above one real navigation bar; translate the whole nav on scroll and zero banner height only on dismissal to avoid gaps and janky height animation.

nodes.label: Inline Command Search Pill
nodes.rationale: Expose search visibly for newcomers while retaining Command-K or Control-K access for power users; the modal must implement focus, Escape, backdrop, arrow-key, Enter, and body-scroll behavior.

nodes.label: Canonical SaaS Three-Section Navigation
nodes.rationale: Use for SaaS, product, and developer-tool pages with several destinations and one primary action; preserve a centered link cluster, frost on scroll, and collapse links before they collide with the brand or CTA.

nodes.label: Floating Navigation Chip
nodes.rationale: Use a small fixed corner chip when a traditional navigation bar would compete with fold-heavy content.

nodes.label: Side-Rail Navigation
nodes.rationale: Use a narrow fixed vertical rail with a rotated wordmark and section indicators for long, numbered editorial or portfolio pages.

nodes.label: Hidden Command-Palette Navigation
nodes.rationale: Hide navigation behind Command-K only for keyboard-first technical audiences who already understand the affordance.

nodes.label: Floating Pill Navigation
nodes.rationale: Use a detached, content-sized blurred pill over a distinct hero surface; if it approaches viewport width or roughly 720px, reduce links or switch navigation patterns.

nodes.label: Newspaper Masthead
nodes.rationale: Reserve the centered wordmark, issue line, link row, and double rule vocabulary for editorial or magazine-shaped pages rather than B2B products.

nodes.label: Brutal Slab Navigation
nodes.rationale: Use heavy borders, uppercase typography, dense rhythm, and square geometry for brutal or declarative brands; rounded corners, soft shadows, and backdrop blur conflict with this vocabulary.

nodes.label: Terminal Command Navigation
nodes.rationale: Use CLI prompt and flag vocabulary only for genuine terminal or developer-tool brands; the blinking cursor is meaningful here because it signals where typing continues.

nodes.label: Edge-Aligned Minimal Navigation
nodes.rationale: Use only a hard-left wordmark and hard-right CTA when a luxury or quiet brand can make empty space carry the design; adding middle links defeats the pattern.

nodes.label: Left-Margin Numbered Heading
nodes.rationale: Use a narrow numbered-label column beside a wide content column for editorial or specimen layouts.

nodes.label: Hanging Heading
nodes.rationale: Place the heading in generous negative space without rules when content needs a quiet, room-to-breathe cadence.

nodes.label: Sticky Pinned Heading
nodes.rationale: Keep headings visible as dense content scrolls, but offset them below sticky navigation and maintain a lower z-index so section headings never paint over the nav.

nodes.label: Sticky Pairing Rule
nodes.rationale: Whenever a sticky top header, nav, or banner exists, declare a matching banner-height token and a sticky-nav z-index at least one level above the in-page sticky z-index.

nodes.label: Inline No-Break Heading
nodes.rationale: Embed a small-caps heading inside body flow when prose continuity matters more than spatial section separation.

nodes.label: Bottom-Anchored Heading
nodes.rationale: Place the label beneath the section when content should be the primary act and its label should read as a footer.

nodes.label: Pull-Quote with Marginalia
nodes.rationale: Use a wide quote column with attribution in a narrow margin only when the page already has an editorial marginalia rhythm.

nodes.label: Hairline Logo Wall
nodes.rationale: Present recognizable customer logos quietly as a monochrome row divided by hairlines, avoiding card boxes and shadows.

nodes.label: Single Huge Quote
nodes.rationale: Give one exceptional quote an entire centered section with only a restrained small-caps attribution beneath it.

nodes.label: Numbered Stat Strip
nodes.rationale: Use a single horizontal row of three to five complementary metrics with tabular numbers rather than treating one number as a hero.

nodes.label: Semantic Design Tokens
nodes.rationale: Centralize tokens and name them by semantic role so design decisions stay coherent and portable rather than encoding raw values in names.

nodes.label: Global Stylesheet Preservation
nodes.rationale: Treat an existing global stylesheet as append-only, preserve framework directives and import ordering, and reuse existing tokens unless the user explicitly authorizes a rewrite.

nodes.label: Instructional Error Messages
nodes.rationale: Errors should state what happened, explain why when known, and give a concrete recovery action.

nodes.label: Custom Craft
nodes.source_location: Custom craft — how to hand-build hero artwork

nodes.label: WebGL Justification Rule
nodes.rationale: Three.js is justified only when interactive 3D is the hero value; non-interactive objects should use lighter media.

nodes.label: Bespoke Custom Depth
nodes.source_location: Bespoke depth — custom that designs the whole page

nodes.label: Opt-In Design-System Locking
nodes.rationale: The system is locked only after explicit user intent because early builds usually iterate and should not prematurely freeze weak decisions.

nodes.label: Floating Navigation Cross-Fade Morph
nodes.source_location: Floating nav on scroll — the cross-fade morph

nodes.label: Constant-Height Navigation Morph
nodes.rationale: The bar and floating modes must have equal total height so changing state does not shift page content.

nodes.label: Hero Enrichment
nodes.source_location: Hero enrichment — when, what, and how much

nodes.label: Image-Need Detection
nodes.rationale: Typography-only is the default; enrichment must communicate information the typography cannot and match the brief's actual media needs.

nodes.label: Hero Polish Patterns
nodes.source_location: Hero shape polish — patterns beyond enrichment

nodes.label: No-Layout-Shift Input States
nodes.rationale: Border thickness and geometry stay constant across input states; state changes use color, outline, or shadow so focus and validation never move layout.

nodes.label: Undo Over Confirm
nodes.rationale: Reversible actions should execute optimistically with a timed Undo instead of interrupting users with confirmation dialogs.

nodes.label: Safe Page-Edge Clipping
nodes.rationale: Global overflow-x clip preserves deliberate visual overflow without horizontal scrolling or the sticky/focus problems caused by overflow hidden.

nodes.label: Macrostructure Diversification
nodes.rationale: Consecutive Hallmark outputs must use different page shapes so distinct briefs do not become color swaps of the same template.

nodes.label: Stat-Led Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: A defensible metric anchors the narrative and must be paired with words explaining what the number means.

nodes.label: Photographic Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: Use full-bleed real photography as page architecture when the product is primarily a feeling; avoid synthetic stock.

nodes.label: Quote-Led Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: Lead with a real attributed customer voice when social proof is the primary unlock; fabricated testimonials destroy trust.

nodes.label: Specimen Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: Reserve the numbered typographic specimen-sheet structure for explicitly editorial or type-foundry briefs; it is banned as a vague default.

nodes.label: Catalogue Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: Treat equal inventory variants uniformly; avoid for narrative products that require hierarchy.

nodes.label: Letter Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: Use intimate first-person prose for personal announcements and appeals, not transactional commerce.

nodes.label: Index-First Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: Make navigation itself the design for browsing-oriented documentation, archives, and knowledge hubs.

nodes.label: Narrative Workflow Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: A real multi-stage product process can be explained as a numbered timeline with one visual per stage.

nodes.label: Split Studio Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: Alternate paired text and proof panels when every claim benefits from visual evidence.

nodes.label: Feature Stack Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: Sticky copy and scroll-synced imagery create controlled pacing for complex premium product stories, but require a strong mobile fallback.

nodes.label: Type Specimen Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: Typography becomes imagery only when a distinctive custom typeface is itself the product or proof.

nodes.label: Portfolio Grid Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: Filterable project cards suit creative service businesses whose work is the pitch, not single products.

nodes.label: Map Diagram Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: Use a spatial node-and-edge composition for systems and territories that are better understood spatially than linearly.

nodes.label: Ecosystem Index Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: Multiple discovery rails suit community and marketplace platforms whose value is emergence and browsing.

nodes.label: Component Playground Macrostructure
nodes.rationale: Interactive preview-and-code blocks are utility content for design systems and documentation, not marketing pitch sections.

nodes.label: Microinteraction Four-Part Model
nodes.rationale: A crafted microinteraction defines trigger, rules, feedback, and loops or modes.

nodes.label: Silent Success
nodes.rationale: Visible successful effects should not generate redundant celebratory toasts.

nodes.label: Optimistic Update with Rollback
nodes.rationale: Mutate predictable local state immediately, then animate rollback and offer recovery only if the request fails.

nodes.label: Reduced Motion as First-Class State
nodes.rationale: Every interaction must explicitly collapse spatial motion while preserving functional state changes.

nodes.label: Keyboard First Hover Second
nodes.rationale: Every hover affordance requires a focus or keyboard equivalent.

nodes.label: Hallmark Motion Language
nodes.rationale: One perceptually meaningful orchestrated moment is preferable to scattered decorative animation.

nodes.label: Compositor-Safe Motion
nodes.rationale: Animate transform and opacity to avoid layout-triggering motion.

nodes.label: Mobile-First Responsiveness
nodes.rationale: Start with the smallest viewport and add layout at content-driven rem breakpoints.

nodes.label: Single-Line Clickable Affordances
nodes.rationale: Shorten or reflow navigation before allowing buttons, CTAs, or primary links to wrap.

nodes.label: Image Grid Track Safety
nodes.rationale: Image-bearing fractional tracks use minmax(0, 1fr) to prevent intrinsic-width overflow.

nodes.label: Pre-Emit Self-Critique
nodes.rationale: Score philosophy, hierarchy, execution, specificity, restraint, and variety before running pass/fail gates; revise any axis below three.

nodes.label: Honest Copy Gate
nodes.rationale: Never fabricate quantitative claims to fill a visual proof slot.

nodes.label: Reuse Real UI Chrome Gate
nodes.rationale: Use real screenshots or omit browser and device chrome instead of redrawing familiar interface shells.

nodes.label: Token Discipline Gate
nodes.rationale: All colors and fonts in an artifact must consume named theme tokens rather than improvise values mid-render.

nodes.label: Structural Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: A page shape is formed by one choice from heading placement, body composition, divider language, button voice, image treatment, and reveal pattern.

nodes.label: Structural Anti-Repetition Rule
nodes.rationale: Consecutive pages should differ on at least three of six structural axes.

nodes.label: Design DNA Study
nodes.rationale: Extract transferable macrostructure, archetypes, type roles, color anchor, and rhythm without copying pixels or signature artwork.

nodes.label: Design.md Emission Consent
nodes.rationale: Portable extraction from a URL requires authorship or permission attestation because emission is more extractive than diagnosis.

nodes.label: Carnival Theme
nodes.rationale: A decorative loud-maximalist editorial system built from tinted paper, variable display type, ornaments, hard-offset shadows, and competing duo-tone accents.

nodes.label: Cobalt Theme
nodes.rationale: A cool, modern-minimal developer-tool register using engineered near-white paper, one electric cobalt signal, hairline structure, and code as the focal element.

nodes.label: Code as Hero
nodes.rationale: Developer-product pages should establish credibility through a concrete API request, response, or terminal demonstration rather than generic marketing imagery.

nodes.label: Working Command Palette
nodes.rationale: The visible Command-K affordance must open an accessible, focus-managed, keyboard-navigable palette rather than serving as decorative chrome.

nodes.label: Hum Theme
nodes.rationale: A playful warm-cream register built from rounded sans typography, multiple accents, soft lifting surfaces, and responsive characterful motion.

nodes.label: Multi-Accent Surface System
nodes.rationale: Pear, cyan, and coral each own distinct semantic surfaces and never blend into cross-accent gradients, preventing a playful palette from becoming visual noise.

nodes.label: Physical Button Press Feedback
nodes.rationale: Buttons lift through a full-width edge shadow on hover and depress downward on activation; scale and spring overshoot are excluded because they weaken the physical press metaphor.

nodes.label: Hum Not-AI Discipline
nodes.rationale: Shared tokens and components form a system, while page architecture, back-half sequencing, card physics, and one designed exception must vary so builds do not become color-swapped templates.

nodes.label: Lumen Theme
nodes.rationale: A premium technical AI-tool register centered on one hand-engineered apparatus, lowercase classical-serif prose, uppercase mono readouts, and calibrated measurement graphics.

nodes.label: Lumen Night Foundry
nodes.rationale: The dark violet drop uses molten brass and a subtly pulsing apparatus whose contained light suggests an instrument actively producing output.

nodes.label: Lumen Day Foundry
nodes.rationale: The cool-bone drop uses indigo and a once-revealed static prism or lens apparatus whose light is measured through refraction rather than emission.

nodes.label: Lumen Apparatus Family
nodes.rationale: Each page constructs exactly one brief-specific CSS and SVG instrument with real leader-line values; generic glowing orbs, placed images, rotation, and duplicate apparatuses are rejected.

nodes.label: Lumen Two-Register Typography
nodes.rationale: All prose renders lowercase while technical mono labels render uppercase; exactly one verb in a headline receives a coral color and persistent underline without italic styling.

nodes.label: Two Plus One Font Rule
nodes.rationale: Use a display and body family with at most one tightly scoped outlier; three families is the ceiling and the outlier may serve no more than two placements.

nodes.label: Ratio-Based Type Scale
nodes.rationale: Typography sizes should follow a selected ratio, headline caps should respond to copy length, and pages should use no more than five sizes.

nodes.label: Font License Rule
nodes.rationale: Free font pairings are canonical; paid foundry faces may enter code only after the user confirms the relevant license.

nodes.label: Structural Fingerprint Audit
nodes.rationale: A centered hero, three equal feature cards, CTA, and footer without asymmetry is a critical template signal even if its visual styling is competent; declared stamps must match what shipped.

nodes.label: Design-System Compliance Audit
nodes.rationale: When design.md exists, audits treat theme drift, family violations, stamp mismatches, and missing system references as explicit findings.

nodes.label: Non-Destructive Redesign Rule
nodes.rationale: Visual redesign defaults to in-place or additive changes and preserves routes, component trees, logic, and source documents unless deletion or rebuild scope is explicitly approved.

nodes.label: Multi-Page Design-System Flow
nodes.rationale: A multi-page redesign first inventories the app, proposes a single design.md system, waits for confirmation, then applies consistent theme and typography with bounded structural variation across page families.

nodes.label: Single-Page Redesign Flow
nodes.rationale: A single-page redesign preserves intent, information architecture, brand, actions, logic, and ownership boundaries while deliberately replacing the structural fingerprint, component voice, reveals, and rhythm.

nodes.label: Creative Variance Engine
nodes.rationale: Select one texture and one layout archetype per build, with aggressive mobile collapse, to prevent repeated premium designs from sharing an identical composition.

nodes.label: Double-Bezel Architecture
nodes.rationale: Major containers use concentric outer and inner enclosures to create machined depth rather than sitting flat on the page.

nodes.label: Fluid Motion Choreography
nodes.rationale: Navigation, buttons, and scroll entry should communicate mass through custom easing, interpolation, and stagger rather than default transitions or instant changes.

nodes.label: Visual Performance Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Animate transform and opacity, limit blur to fixed or sticky layers, isolate noise overlays, and reserve z-index values for defined system layers.

nodes.label: Next.js Documentation Rule
nodes.rationale: Because the installed Next.js version may break training-era conventions, agents must consult the bundled version-specific documentation before writing code.

nodes.label: Astryx UI Workflow
nodes.rationale: UI work must discover an Astryx kit, inspect templates and component contracts, frame layouts with system components, use semantic tokens, and self-check against hand-rolled layout and raw values.

nodes.label: High-Volume Query Integration Boundary
nodes.rationale: The current bounded RLS query facade supports the shell, while production-scale history should move to aggregate RPCs and cursor-based ledger pagination without exposing a service key or unbounded client fetch.
